answer.generated: Back-propagation applies the chain rule to compute gradients by propagating errors backward through the network. Specifically, it computes ∂ℒ/∂θ for each parameter θ by multiplying the gradient of the loss with respect to the corresponding activation z (e.g., ∂ℒ/∂z) by the derivative of z with respect to θ (e.g., ∂z/∂θ). This allows efficient computation of gradients even in deep architectures, enabling weight updates via gradient descent. The key idea is that the gradient of the loss with respect to any variable is obtained by multiplying the gradient of the loss with respect to the next variable by the derivative of the next variable with respect to the current one, recursively.
